indicators.note: recycling breaks material down and remakes it, so the letters of the two words before are remade into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some smart spot is the right place to take one's waste for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recycle' reworks the letters of SMART PLACE; the whole clue then describes what you would take to such a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded iron and steel taken for reprocessing is exactly the stuff a recycling place handles.

clue.text: One may be up for a shower

definitions.text: One may be up for a shower

parts.words: One may be up for a shower
parts.note: reads like a person keen to bathe, but describes a thing raised against rain

explanation.surface: Someone who fancies a wash in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up for' suggests willingness; here it means literally held up, open, when rain falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain canopy carried by hand is put up whenever a shower of rain starts.

definitions.meaning: a single tome of a set is called this
size or amount, as in the quantity of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one book of a series and the amount of space or quantity something takes up.

definitions.meaning: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted
a colloquial sense: urinated, as in 'went to the loo'

explanation.walkthrough: 'went' looks like plain going away; it is the coy euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden pest plant, and also the informal past tense of the verb for passing water.

clue.text: Very unlikely to be imported from across the world

definitions.meaning: implausible, hard to believe

definitions.text: to be imported from across the world
definitions.meaning: literally brought from a distant place, read as two words

explanation.surface: Goods shipped from the other side of the globe seem improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means implausible, and taken literally describes something brought in from a distant land.

clue.text: Something to eat in the Tube

definitions.text: Something to eat in the Tube

parts.words: Something to eat in the Tube
parts.note: suggests a snack on the London Underground, but means a food in the form of a tube

explanation.surface: A snack eaten while riding London's Underground railway, known as the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T points to London's Underground; the food is simply tube-shaped pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian pasta comes as short hollow tubes, so it is literally an edible tube.

indicators.note: read as re-markable, able to be marked again in a new form, so the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The glory of an outstanding outcome, as of a match or exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory or brilliance, as in adding lustre to a reputation; a synonym of splendour.

definitions.meaning: to produce young, as in to bring forth children
a large furry mammal such as a grizzly

explanation.surface: A creature delivering its young.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bring forth offspring, and the noun is a large heavy mammal such as the grizzly.

clue.text: These days, answer to no lord

parts.note: someone without a title is a commoner

explanation.surface: A modern claim that nowadays nobody need bow to a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The secular name for the current calendar era since year 1, used in place of AD, so it covers the present age.

parts.note: cute can mean shrewd or clever, as in 'a cute move'

explanation.surface: Describing a smart approach to a problem, a clever angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of less than ninety degrees is given this name in geometry.

parts.note: sounds like a groping hand, but describes a ship whose keel rests on the seabed

explanation.surface: Someone patting a backside, inappropriately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' suggests a backside; for a vessel it is the sea floor, and the answer splits as A plus GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded ship has its hull resting on the shore or seabed, stuck in shallow water.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to praise insincerely to win favour
more level, less bumpy

explanation.surface: A liquid hand wash leaves the skin silkier.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to praise insincerely, and the comparative adjective means more level or even.

indicators.note: the author sits inside the run of letters across the two following words

explanation.surface: Asking whether some writer used the Tamil language, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the name across TAMIL NEVER. A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English writer who created Winnie-the-Pooh, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: Sort of jelly prepared in our temple

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new form, as a dish is prepared

explanation.surface: A jelly offering made ready in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaseline is the familiar brand of the soft greasy jelly refined from crude oil.

definitions.meaning: the day on which gifts are given, read as a gift day
the current era, the time we live in

explanation.definitionFit: Read whole it means the current time; split up, it describes 25 December, the day of gifts.

clue.text: State parting two friends to a significant degree

indicators.note: the state pushes the two friends apart by sitting between them

parts.note: a mate and an ally are both friends
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A government separating two pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' says the state splits the pair of friends; RI is Rhode Island, a common crossword abbreviation for an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means substantially or considerably, as in 'materially different'.

clue.text: Be very annoyed, getting oneself distressed?

definitions.meaning: to be extremely frustrated or exasperated
read as dis-tressed: removing one's own tresses, that is pulling locks from one's head

explanation.surface: Someone becoming upset and working themselves into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' looks like upset; the question mark invites the reading 'deprived of tresses'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be frantic with frustration, and literally describes pulling out one's own locks.

clue.text: Leaving, having finished with hurt feelings

parts.note: off means departing, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: Someone walking out after finishing, nursing wounded pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset or insulted by a remark has had their feelings hurt.

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order, as if arranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Violet buying a heating appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic appliance that burns paraffin to warm a room is a kind of heater.

clue.text: Walked out of game? In the US that would be bizarre

definitions.meaning: left the pitch or playing area, read as two words
unconventional or odd, from the US baseball phrase 'out of ...'

explanation.surface: A player quitting a match, which Americans would find strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the US' flags the American origin: left field is a baseball position, and 'out of left field' means unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the term means unconventional or strange, from baseball slang.

definitions.meaning: a call to go more quickly
what a person abstaining from food could say of themselves

explanation.surface: A hungry person urging others along because they have no food.
explanation.definitionFit: The word urges more speed, and also names one who abstains from food, as in Lent or Ramadan.

clue.text: To some extent very large and sunny

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, its ending cut away

explanation.surface: Describing weather that is partly vast and bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' trims GE from SO LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the sun, as in solar power drawn from sunshine.

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: to err is to do wrong

explanation.surface: An anxious person gulping the wrong beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from southern Spain is a common after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Sort of stockings an old trout could get into?

definitions.meaning: hosiery woven in an open mesh

definitions.text: an old trout could get into?
definitions.meaning: an old woman, called an old trout, could wear these, and a real trout could be caught in a mesh net

explanation.surface: A cruel joke about an older woman squeezing into racy hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old trout' is British slang for an unpleasant older woman, but a fish could literally get into a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-mesh hosiery is named after the netting used to catch fish.

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Uniting in good jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To meld or weld two things into one, as metals melted together.

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Choosing colour schemes for fresh floor coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: The bands of colours produced when light is split by a prism are plural of spectrum.

indicators.note: the agent spans the river, holding it inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A nimble spy getting over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and nimble, especially of an older person; a synonym of agile.

clue.text: Riddle one's spun the previous day

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one is I, and 's is read as is, shortened to S
eve is the day before, as Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A puzzle someone made up yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' acts on the 'one's' piece only. 'Riddle' is not a puzzle here: as a noun it is a coarse garden sifter.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve for sifting soil, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: On the surface, it's no way to proceed

definitions.text: On the surface, it's no way to proceed

parts.words: On the surface, it's no way to proceed
parts.note: sounds like a dismissive judgement, but means that this way of getting about does not use the ground

explanation.surface: Something that looks, at first glance, like a bad way to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the surface' seems to mean 'apparently'; read literally, flying is not a surface journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying from place to place is a journey made above the ground, not over its surface.
